# Results — Study 524 (Operating-Leverage) on the real survivor basket

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Signal: operating leverage
OL = OperatingCosts_t / Total_Assets_t, from SEC EDGAR companyfacts
(`CostOfGoodsAndServicesSold`/`CostOfRevenue` + `SellingGeneralAndAdministrativeExpense`,
`Assets`). Forward returns from Yahoo daily adjusted prices. As-of **2026-06-27**.*

**Definition**:
- OL_t = (COGS_t + SG&A_t) / Total_Assets_t  (higher = more operating-cost-intensive)

**Prediction (Novy-Marx 2011)**: HIGH OL → HIGH future returns (an operating-risk premium
that overlaps the value effect). We go **long high-OL / short low-OL** (g3 − g1).

**Execution lag (one)**: OL from fiscal year y drives a 12-month forward total return that
*begins 4 months after the fiscal-year-end* (when the 10-K is public) and is entered at the
close 1 trading day later. A forward window is used only if it has fully completed by the
as-of date — no partial period is ever stamped.

**Universe**: a fixed ~40-name large-cap **survivor** basket; ~38 names/year carry the EDGAR
operating-cost + assets tags. **Survivorship-biased** — every firm survived to 2026.

**Window**: 17 signal years (2008–2024), forecasting 12-month returns 2009–2026.

**SURVIVORSHIP-BIAS WARNING**: the basket is large-cap names still trading in 2026.
High-operating-leverage firms whose demand collapsed and went under are absent. All results
are upper bounds on a live strategy.

## Tercile returns (OL low to high, 12-month forward)

| Tercile | Mean return | Sharpe | HAC t-stat | Hit rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **g1 (low OL — capital-heavy)** | **+22.3%/yr** | +0.99 | +4.68 | 94% |
| g2 (mid OL) | +16.0%/yr | +1.23 | +6.69 | 100% |
| **g3 (high OL — operating-leverage)** | **+20.1%/yr** | +1.30 | +5.96 | 100% |
| Equal-weight market | +19.5%/yr | +1.42 | +8.01 | 100% |

## Long high-OL / short low-OL hedge (g3 − g1)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Mean annual return | **−2.14%/yr** |
| Sharpe ratio | −0.10 |
| HAC Newey-West t-stat | **−0.39** |
| Hit rate (positive years) | 59% (10/17 years) |
| n (years) | 17 |

The hedge points the *wrong way*: the low-OL tercile (+22.3%/yr) actually nudges past the
high-OL tercile (+20.1%/yr), so the long-high/short-low book loses a small −2.14%/yr.

## Excess vs equal-weight market

| Arm | Excess return | HAC t-stat |
|---|--:|--:|
| High-OL (g3) | +0.6%/yr | +0.31 |
| Low-OL (g1) | +2.8%/yr | +0.75 |

Neither leg clears |t| ≥ 2 vs the equal-weight market: there is no operating-leverage tilt
to exploit in either direction.

## Placebo / label-shuffle null (1000 shuffles)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Real hedge mean | −2.14%/yr |
| Shuffle mean | −0.12%/yr |
| Shuffle std | 3.19%/yr |
| Placebo p (P[shuffle ≥ real]) | **0.720** |

The real hedge sits inside (in fact slightly left of) the shuffle distribution — a randomly
relabelled OL signal would do better 72% of the time.

## Random-portfolio null (500 draws/year)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Random-control mean | +0.11%/yr (zero in expectation) |
| Random-control std | 7.8%/yr |
| High-OL beats random draw | **54%** of 500×17yr draws (chance level) |

## Costs (gross vs net)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Gross hedge | −2.14%/yr |
| Trading drag (10 bps × 2.0 turnover) | −0.20%/yr |
| Borrow drag (50 bps short leg) | −0.50%/yr |
| **Net hedge** | **−2.84%/yr** |

The already-negative gross hedge only worsens once costs and short borrow are charged.

## Synthetic positive control (seed-robust, 25 seeds)

| Planted premium | Mean hedge | Mean HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|
| +0.00/yr (null) | +0.1%/yr | +0.15 |
| +0.06/yr | +13.2%/yr | +15.16 |
| +0.10/yr | +21.9%/yr | +25.06 |

The engine recovers a planted operating-leverage effect with a large, seed-robust t-stat,
and the null behaves (t ≈ 0). The real-tape null is therefore a statement about the
**market and the survivor basket**, not the method.

## Verdict

The predicted effect (high operating leverage → high returns) is **absent** — in fact
mildly inverted — on this survivor basket. The long-high-OL / short-low-OL hedge earns
**−2.14%/yr** with HAC *t* = **−0.39**, indistinguishable from zero and pointing the wrong
way. The placebo p = **0.720** (a shuffled label beats the real signal 72% of the time), the
high-OL leg beats only **54%** of random same-size draws (chance), and the already-negative
gross hedge worsens to **−2.84%/yr net** once costs and short borrow are charged.

The synthetic control proves the engine is faithful: planting a +6%/yr operating-leverage
effect yields HAC *t* ≈ +15 (seed-robust over 25 seeds), and the null behaves (*t* ≈ 0). So
the absence on the real tape is a property of the market and the basket, not the method.

Two honest reasons the academic premium does not appear here:

1. **Wrong universe.** Novy-Marx (2011) estimates operating leverage on the broad US
   cross-section, where the premium overlaps value and bites hardest among small and
   mid-caps with limited access to capital. On ~38 heavily-covered large caps the
   operating-risk premium is thin and arbitraged.
2. **Survivorship selection.** Operating leverage is, by construction, a *risk* premium: it
   is meant to pay for the bad states where a high-fixed-cost firm sees demand collapse and
   operating profit cratered. On a survivor basket those bad-state failures are deleted, so
   the high-OL group is dominated by firms whose demand *didn't* collapse — exactly the
   sample where the operating-risk premium should be smallest (note 2015/2022/2024: the
   low-OL, capital-light megacaps ran away from the high-OL retailers and industrials).

- **Signal — NONE** (hedge *t* = −0.39, wrong sign; placebo p = 0.72; beats 54% of random
  draws; literature supports the premium for a broad non-biased universe, not survivor
  large-caps).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE** (negative gross edge; −2.84%/yr net after costs and borrow;
  nothing to trade).
- **Operating- vs financial-leverage channel — BUSTED** (the fixed-cost / operating-leverage
  channel is no more present than the balance-sheet financial-leverage channel of
  [Study 154](../../154-leverage-anomaly/); both vanish on the survivor large-cap panel).
